To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the intramolecular reaction in a supercoiled DNA chain is diffusion controlled, and (ii) the diffusion is essentially one-dimensional.

the intrachain reactions between the superhelix end loops of supercoiled circular DNA are diffusion controlled and that the mean time of their first collision is inversley proportional to the reaction size.

the intrachain reactions in supercoiled DNA are diffusion-controlled, and the mean reaction time is inversely proportional, not to the reaction radius R, but to the product R x (1 - alpha), where alpha is the fraction of the reaction time during which the reactive groups are separated by a distance exceeding R.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a diffusion-controlled intrachain reaction of a supercoiled DNA molecule.
a model of intrachain reactions, in which the diffusion of the reactive groups along DNA contour is the limiting step.
the intramolecular reactions of supercooled DNA molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intrachain reaction of a superhelical DNA molecule is controlled by the one-dimensional diffusion of its ends along the contour.

the diffusion-controlled intramolecule reaction of supercooled DNA is a complex process, in which one-dimensional diffusion is the main mechanism, but the three-dimensional diffusion is also present and may be important for some cases.
, for a DNA chain in a solution of physiological salt concentration, the intrachain reactions can occur at a rate that is comparable to the rate of reactions of free DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Brownian Dynamics simulations provide a good qualitative description of the intramolecular reaction in supercoiled DNA and allow one to make quantitative predictions for a number of reaction parameters.
the diffusion-controlled intrachain reaction of supercooled DNA can be treated by a simple one-dimensional model, provided the reactive groups are separated by a large distance.
the Brownian Dynamics simulations of the superhelical DNA conformations can be successfully used to study the intramolecular reactions in supercoiled DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion-controlled intrachain reaction is a very efficient process, which can be used in DNA-based molecular machines.
the Brownian Dynamics simulations are a powerful tool for modeling diffusion-controlled intrachain chemical reactions in supercoiled DNA.

the diffusion of the DNA superhelices in solution can be described as one-dimensional diffusion along the DNA contour, which is a much simpler model than the three-dimensional diffusion of the whole superhelix.
